1491
Start by unlearning
the empty continent.
North America is full — millions of people, cities bigger than London.

FIRST QUESTION
Was there ever one single
"Native American culture"?

Not even close.
Hundreds of nations. The environment wrote the rules for every one of them.

THREE REGIONS

Southwest

Adobe villages, irrigation

Plains

Bison, tipis, movement

Northeast

Longhouses, rivers, corn

caption: Pueblo · Arid Southwest
Adobe villages, irrigation canals — corn, beans, and squash pulled out of dry ground. That’s engineering.
beats.anim_prompt: Slow aerial drift over an adobe pueblo village at golden hour, thin chimney smoke rising, desert mountains behind. No people in focus.

caption: Plains · Open Grassland
Bison on foot — no horses yet. Portable tipis, dried meat, moving with the seasons.
Northeast · Woodlands & Rivers
Palisaded towns, longhouses — corn in summer, hunting and fishing the rest of the year.

beats.anim_prompt: Aerial drone glide over large ancient earthen mounds in a green river valley at dawn, thin mist, birds. Monumental, quiet.

beats.html:
THE ENGINE
Maize — the crop that makes
complex society possible.

INVENTED, NOT FOUND
Wild teosinte
→ maize
Bred over thousands of years, carried north century by century.
No maize, no Cahokia. It’s that simple.

EVIDENCE
How do we actually know
all this?

THE RECORD
  • The mounds, the burials
  • Trade goods that don’t belong to the local geology
  • Early French explorers — who asked, and wrote down the answers

PUEBLO · VILLAGE-BASED
Each adobe town
runs its own affairs
Tied to neighbors by trade and ceremony.
The kiva — underground ceremonial chamber — as civic heart.

IROQUOIS · THE CONFEDERACY
Five nations.
One Great Law of Peace.
Consensus council. Clan mothers choose the chiefs.
Debated: did Franklin’s generation borrow the federal idea?

beats.chain_caption: Walk the chain with two regions — the comparison writes itself.

beats.html:
MYTH TO BUST
"Native peoples lived in harmony with nature
and left no trace."
True?
beats.anim_prompt: Prairie grass fire flame front creeping across tallgrass at dusk, embers lifting into a darkening sky. Controlled, natural.

beats.html:
CRONON · CHANGES IN THE LAND
Not pristine.
Engineered.
Burned underbrush, cleared fields, planted chestnuts.
The "wilderness" the settlers found was a garden — and a graveyard.

THE THESIS
Diversity wasn’t the exception.
It was the story.
Environment → food → society → government. One continent, hundreds of answers.
beats.anim_prompt: Slow push-in over ancient earthen mounds and a wide river at morning, light haze. Sense of a vanished city.

QUESTION 1 OF 3
The crop that made settled life possible north of Mexico?

QUESTION 1 OF 3
The crop that made settled life possible north of Mexico?

Maize — corn. Bred from wild teosinte, carried north over centuries.

QUESTION 2 OF 3
The confederacy of five nations under the Great Law of Peace?

QUESTION 2 OF 3
The confederacy of five nations under the Great Law of Peace?

The Iroquois — the Haudenosaunee. Consensus council, matrilineal clans.

QUESTION 3 OF 3
True or false: pre-contact America was untouched wilderness.

QUESTION 3 OF 3
True or false: pre-contact America was untouched wilderness.

False. Burned, cleared, planted, and engineered.
